title: GitLab CI regular expression compilation permits unauthenticated server code execution
summary: An integer overflow in the CI/CD regular expression compiler can, under certain conditions, allow an unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code on an affected GitLab CE or EE server through a crafted regular expression.

severity.rationale: An unauthenticated remote attacker can execute code in CI infrastructure. The published vector requires neither privileges nor user interaction.

exposure: Relevant to affected self-managed installations. GitLab states its hosted and Dedicated environments were patched before the release notice.

params.instructions: Read the GitLab server version and compare its branch against the fixed floors 19.2.8, 19.3.5 and 19.4.2.

remediation.action: Contain exposure and apply a verified fix
remediation.details: Upgrade using the supported GitLab upgrade path to the latest patched release on a supported branch. The listed versions are minimum fixes for this CVE, not a complete current security baseline.
remediation.risk: Medium. Server upgrades require backups, supported upgrade steps and service validation.

verification: Confirm the GitLab server reports 19.2.8, 19.3.5, 19.4.2 or a later patched release on its branch.

review.notes: Independent reviewer re-read every tier 1 source and checked every field. No open findings.

history.change: Initial record drafted for independent review.
Named the integer overflow in the CI/CD regular expression compiler, qualified the triggering conditions and made verification specific to the patched server version.
